cells.gaps: No row states which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, and nothing on the HMIS is dated after January 2022: whether the decentralisation to district and primary level then planned has happened is not established, nor whether DHIS2 carries routine patients-treated reporting rather than surveillance and immunisation aggregates. Governance facts are all from January 2022, outside the 36 months, and the plan they name ran 2020-2024, so no governance value has been found; the only digitised facts are a 2018 rating of no electronic aggregate entry at district level (MUS-027) and a 2020 statement on Rodrigues alone (MUS-035).
cells.note: DHIS2 was being implemented as the national health information system and used at regional and national level only, with primary-level entry still a plan (MUS-023, MUS-026). Stage 3 needs a district-keyed system taking the clinics' reports, which no row shows.

cells.gaps: About thirty public facilities of the East and Centre run e-Health in pilot (MUS-037, October 2026), but primary clinics are not counted apart from hospitals, so no share or count of primary clinics is established. Owner is disputed inside the window: UNDP in charge of procurement and overall management (MUS-006, MUS-013) against the ministry and its Digital Health Company (MUS-014, MUS-020). The only plan named ran 2020-2024 and has ended, and the source of the MUR 600 million is not stated. Rows MUS-001 to MUS-005 are from the excluded source and set nothing.
cells.note: e-Health holds one national record per patient retrievable at any connected facility, but in October 2026 it is still a pilot in about thirty facilities of two regions, which is pilot sites. Stage 3 needs most T1 and T2 hospitals or primary clinics in some districts past a pilot, which no row shows.
